extracted.intended_audience: IPR practitioners (petitioners and patent owners), PTAB judges, and USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: An Office of the Director order granting Director Review, vacating part of a PTAB Final Written Decision, and remanding the IPR for further proceedings to address specific claim‑level arguments (here, claim 17) and determine whether the petitioner met the preponderance‑of‑the‑evidence burden for related claims. Includes procedural instructions (joinder, timeline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to consider and address Patent Owner's arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board must consider and address arguments a Patent Owner actually raised regarding patentability (e.g., Patent Owner presented multiple arguments disputing Petitioner's unpatentability contentions for claim 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record shows the Patent Owner raised specific arguments (for example, that a reference discloses time division multiplexing rather than the claimed time division duplex and is silent on claimed beacon messages), the Board must consider those arguments; failure to do so can warrant Director Review and vacatur/in part remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in stating the record
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board should not state that a Patent Owner 'does not present any arguments' when the record demonstrates otherwise (the Decision's statement that Patent Owner 'does not present any arguments specific to claims 2, 9, and 17' was found erroneous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before relying on such statements as a basis for a decision, the Board must ensure its characterization of the record is correct; erroneous characterizations may require vacatur and remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in IPR — preponderance of the evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must show unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence (the Board shall determine whether Petitioner has shown by a preponderance of the evidence that claims 2 and 9 are unpatentable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when claims are addressed together because they share limitations, the Board must determine whether the petitioner has met the preponderance‑of‑the‑evidence burden for each asserted claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand instruction to evaluate specific claim limitations against asserted grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Director Review is granted because the Board omitted addressing arguments, the Board is instructed to consider the Patent Owner's arguments as to the specific claim (here, claim 17) under the identified grounds (here, Grounds 3 and 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On remand the Board must evaluate whether the asserted references actually teach the claimed limitations (e.g., whether Amit teaches TDD or only time division multiplexing, and whether DSL‑Book's pilot tones suggest claimed beacon messages) and explain its conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility and notation of joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional party (DIRECTV, LLC) who filed a petition in another IPR was joined as a petitioner to this case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joinder of additional petitioners may be recorded in the proceeding; orders may reflect such procedural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board need not repeat every argument but must address material issues
rubrics_metrics.description: There is 'no legal requirement for [the Board] to restate each argument advanced by a patent owner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Board need not recite every argument verbatim, it must address the arguments that are material to its decision; failing to address material arguments can be reversible or subject to Director Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims that share limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims recite the same limitations (claims 2 and 9 recite the same limitations as claim 17), the Board may address them together but still must determine whether petitioner has proven unpatentability for each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing claims together is permissible for efficiency, but the Board should still make clear, claim‑by‑claim findings or otherwise ensure the record supports a determination for each claim under the required burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and articulation of obviousness grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground 3 challenges certain claims as obvious over Amit and Jacobsen; Ground 4 challenges certain claims as obvious over Amit, Jacobsen, and DSL‑Book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness grounds must identify the references and combinations relied upon and be evaluated with respect to the specific claim limitations at issue (e.g., TDD protocol, beacon messages). The Board should explain how the combination teaches or renders obvious the claimed limitations or why it does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand timing expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent good cause, the Board shall issue its decision within 30 days of this Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may set firm timelines for the Board to complete further proceedings following remand; extensions require showing good cause.
